key_insight: The paper proposes a framework to validate quantum observable estimates even when classical ground-truth simulation is unavailable, using experiment design and noise-aware bounds to build trust.
engineering_relevance: It supports trustworthy quantum simulation workflows for scientific computing by replacing direct classical verification with principled validation of the estimation process and device noise.
method: Designs a suite of quantum heuristic experiments to test the assumptions behind observable estimates.
Introduces the operator Loschmidt echo to probe semi-scrambling dynamics in an experimentally accessible regime.
Extends validation to accuracy bounds by characterizing and manipulating device noise, effectively validating the noise model.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the framework was applied to a physical model that strains leading classical simulators, and the resulting quantum estimates were judged the most credible among several candidate methods.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful noise characterization and assumptions about the noise model, so validity may weaken if device behavior drifts or is not well captured by the model.
paper_title: Observable Estimation in the Absence of Classical Verification
